text:
Original SASRec retains identity explicitly: its sampler selects `user`, reads `user_train[user]`, builds `set(user_train[user])`, and returns `(user, seq, pos, neg)`. It samples one negative per active position, excluding the complete training history. Proposed adaptation: keep user IDs inside dataset records or the training collator; generate 32 negatives before a diagnostic wrapper exposes `(None, sequence, positive, negative)`. Never reconstruct identity from truncated sequences. Preserve diagnostic tensors as B×L; keep training’s B×L×32 negatives separate. [Original sampler](https://github.com/kang205/SASRec/blob/master/sampler.py)

For each active target, define eligible items as category-local IDs `1..N` minus the complete training-history set and target. Causal-prefix exclusion instead removes only interactions observed through that position plus the target, allowing later training positives as negatives; it therefore does not satisfy complete-history exclusion. Proposed bounded sampler: draw uniform IDs, reject excluded IDs and already accepted negatives, and stop after a fixed proposal budget. If unfinished, construct the exact remaining eligible set in sorted order and fill using `rng.choice(..., replace=False)`. This preserves uniform sampling without replacement. If fewer than 32 eligible items exist, 32 distinct negatives are impossible: use an explicit masked shortfall policy. [NumPy choice](https://numpy.org/doc/stable/reference/random/generated/numpy.random.Generator.choice.html)

Use dedicated seeded generators rather than shared global RNG state. Preserve preprocessing seed 0 and training seed 42; derive category/epoch/worker streams using `SeedSequence`. Worker seeds alone cannot control asynchronous batch arrival: consume batches in deterministic order, or derive generators from stable sample identifiers. Keep eligible arrays ordered and software versions fixed. Neither exclusion policy requires validation/test interactions. [NumPy parallel RNG guidance](https://numpy.org/doc/stable/reference/random/parallel.html)
